messages:
Ashley M: Heads-up — seeing a weird placement pattern in eu-west1 GPU pool since 08:09 UTC, a bunch of 4-GPU jobs stuck Pending for ~40m.
Rahul P: I noticed. Some nodes in rack-17 report 0 allocatable GPUs to the scheduler even though nvidia-smi shows available memory.
Maya S: FYI pasted node labels & taints from one of the problem nodes:
```
kubectl describe node rack-17-node-03
Labels: topology.kubernetes.io/zone=eu-west1-b, rack=rack-17, peerlink-latency=23ms
Taints: egress-qos=throttled:NoSchedule, gpu:maintenance=true:NoExecute
Allocatable: cpu: 32, memory: 250Gi, nvidia.com/gpu: 0
```
Kevin L: That egress-qos taint is new from the network throttling rule we rolled last week. Scheduler's topology/filtering might be excluding those nodes because of our bandwidth-aware scoring.
Ashley M: Also saw scheduler logs with repeated rejections: 
```
E0908 08:10:12 scheduler_pred.go:142] Pod default/large-job-19 failed predicate: topologySpreadConstraints not satisfied
```
Rahul P: TopologySpread complaining is odd — these jobs have preferredDuringScheduling affinity to NVLINK racks. If peerlink latency > 20ms they prefer different nodes and then the scoring pushes them away from rack-17.
Maya S: Quick repro: create a synthetic 4-GPU pod with nodeAffinity required on gpu=true and set --simulate-peerlink-latency=25ms in scheduler config, scheduler avoids rack-17 nodes.
Ashley M: We tried cordon/drain on one node to force reschedule; pods landed on other racks but several failed with CrashLoopBackOff after starting — logs show driver mismatch on one spot instance.
Kevin L: So two separate issues: (1) network egress QoS taint + bandwidth-aware scoring excluding otherwise healthy GPUs; (2) a subset of spot nodes with stale GPU drivers.
Rahul P: Short-term mitigation: patch scoring to deprioritize peerlink penalty for GPU-heavy pods, and add toleration for egress-qos=throttled for our critical batch queue.
Maya S: Proposed rollout plan:
1) Canary change to scheduler config in eu-west1 canary pool (09:30 UTC)
2) Add toleration to batch-4g jobs for egress-qos=throttled for 2h backfill
3) Run driver validation job across warm-pool nodes and mark bad AMIs
```
kubectl apply -f toleration-patch.yaml
# toleration-patch.yaml: tolerations: - key: "egress-qos" operator: "Equal" value: "throttled" effect: "NoSchedule"
```
Kevin L: Cost note — accepting throttled nodes for backfill will increase cross-az egress and latency for some workloads; estimate +12% network egress cost for eu-west1 this week if we backfill aggressively.
Ashley M: That's acceptable for the next 24h to unblock pipelines. Can we rate-limit backfill to not saturate the peerlink?
Rahul P: I'll add a concurrent-scheduling cap via pod disruption budget-like blocker in the batch queue controller. Limits to 6 concurrent 4-GPU pods per rack.
infra-bot: autoscaler: added +2 nodes to eu-west1-warm-pool at 08:15 UTC to compensate for placement failures.
Maya S: I've started the driver-scan job across warm-pool; will post results in ~25m.
Kevin L: After canary, if scoring tweak looks good we'll roll to eu-west1 primary. Tagging @eng-platform for awareness.
Ashley M: Thanks all — I'll monitor PodPending counts and queue latency. Please ping here when canary completes. :thumbsup:
Rahul P: Can confirm canary patch applied to scheduler at 09:32 UTC. Monitoring metrics: pending->running rate improved from 0.4->1.1 pods/min.
Ashley M: Nice, keeping this thread as single source.
